chunks: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said:

Whoever performs wudu (ablution) for the Maghrib prayer, that wudu (ablution) is an atonement for what has passed of his sins during his day, apart from the major sins. And whoever performs wudu (ablution) for the morning prayer, that wudu (ablution) is an atonement for what has passed of his sins during his night, except the major sins.
ai.seo_question: How does wudu (ablution) before Maghrib and Fajr affect a person's sins?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the spiritual merit of wudu (ablution) connected to salat (prayer), especially before Maghrib and Fajr. It states that such wudu (ablution) expiates minor sins committed during the preceding day or night, while major sins are excluded from this expiation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.103 - Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) said:

'Whoever performs ablution for the Maghrib prayer, his ablution serves as atonement for the sins he committed during the day, except for the major sins.
And whoever performs ablution for the Fajr prayer, his ablution serves as atonement for the sins he committed during the night, except for the major sins.'"
